notes: Original Schedule TO-I of Eaton Vance Senior Income Trust (EVF), filed June 29, 2021, with the Offer to Purchase (seq=2), the commencement press release (seq=7) and the Standstill Agreement dated May 12, 2021 (seq=9). EVENT 1, the cef_tender: up to 60% / 22,719,965 Shares at 99% of NAV struck at the close on the expiration date. For context, 37,866,607 Shares were outstanding as of June 23, 2021, and the NAV that day was $6.8923 (fee illustration $6.8234). commencement_date: from the June 29, 2021 joint press release, which 'announced today the commencement' of the offers, and the Offer to Purchase dated June 29, 2021. The same release's boilerplate says 'The Funds have not commenced the Tender Offers described in this release', which contradicts it. The withdrawal right after August 25, 2021 is described as 40 business days from commencement. trigger_origin: the offer and the three conditional tenders came from an agreement between EVM and Saba Capital Management, L.P. made on May 12, 2021. Saba agreed to vote for the new advisory agreement (needed after Morgan Stanley acquired Eaton Vance Corp.), to tender all but one of its Shares in this Offer and in any Subsequent Conditional Tender Offer, and to refrain from proxy solicitations and proposals. EVM bears the offer's costs. conditions (Section 13): the purchase must not (a) delist the shares from the NYSE (listing), (b) cause loss of RIC status (ric_or_tax_status) or (c) breach the asset coverage requirements for senior securities (other). Other conditions are (2a) a legal action challenging the offer (legal_injunction), (2b) a suspension of trading on the exchanges (market_disruption, which also covers (2c) a banking moratorium and (2d) new limits on the extension of credit), and (3) the Board finding a breach of fiduciary duty on written advice of counsel (board_discretion). Shareholder approval of the New Agreement was a condition of the Board's approval of the Offer, but the filing says it was met at the June 24, 2021 special meeting, so it is not listed as an open condition. The offer is not conditioned on any minimum number of Shares, and the Fund expects to borrow part of the purchase cost under a credit agreement with State Street, which is not stated as a financing condition. EVENT 2, the conditional_tender_programme, is a second event disclosed in this filing (Section 9 and the press release), although the Offer to Purchase says it does not relate to it. In Q4 of each of 2022, 2023 and 2024 the Fund tenders for up to 10% of the then-outstanding shares at 98% of NAV if, from January to August of that year, the average discount to NAV exceeds 10%, measured on the volume-weighted average market price and NAV on business days. window_start and window_end are null because the window is stated only as months ('from January to August of that year', in each of 2022-2024). The joint press release says EFT and EFR have the same conditional programme.
